name: IEC SR latch (rectangular form)
summary: Rectangular IEC bistable with S and R inputs that set or reset the stored state immediately.
description: The simplest IEC bistable is a rectangle with inputs labelled S and R and outputs Q and complemented Q. An active S sets the element to 1 and an active R resets it to 0, with no clock involved. Negation or polarity marks show active-low inputs, as on devices built from cross-coupled NAND gates.

SR latches appear in alarm-latching and seal-in logic on control drawings. The key question for a reviewer is what happens when both S and R are active; dependency notation or a note should state whether set or reset dominates.

The symbol does not specify the power-up state. Where it matters, add the I=0 or I=1 qualifier or a note. A separate reset or initialisation circuit is needed when the system requires a defined starting condition.
readingNotes: Check for active-low marks on S and R.
Look for a stated set or reset priority.
drawingChecklist: Label S and R inside the outline.
State the priority when both are active.
Specify the power-up state where relevant.
distinction: A clocked SR flip-flop has 1S and 1R inputs under C1 control; the plain latch has none.
